description.value: An open-label exploratory study investigating baseline grey matter volume differences associated with alcohol relapse and the effect of accelerated high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation on grey matter volume in alcohol-dependent patients.

spans.text: Here we wanted to investigate whether baseline grey matter volume (GMV) can predict relapse and whether 15 accelerated high-frequency (HF)- rTMS sessions may influence GMV in areas related to relapse.

value: Compared to healthy controls, we expected grey matter abnormalities in brain areas frequently reported in alcohol addiction.
In line with previous literature ( ; ), we hypothesized that baseline differences would be present between abstainers and relapsers.
We expected that accelerated HF-rTMS treatment would positively affect GMV most prominently in the abstainers, in particular in regions related to relapse.

description.value: Open-label study in which alcohol-dependent patients received accelerated HF-rTMS and were scanned before and after treatment; relapse was assessed four weeks after stimulation. Healthy controls were included for baseline comparison.
